notes: Conformance run of the legacy app against the expected specification in the Ground Truth.
It is not the Spec_Restoration_Evaluation (AI-restored spec vs Ground Truth) and not the Compatibility_Evaluation (legacy vs modern app).
Expected specification and observed legacy behavior are recorded separately. Expected values are never changed to match observed behavior.
Non-deterministic fields are masked as <non-deterministic>. No wall-clock values are stored, so repeated runs produce identical files.
approved_divergence: the legacy behavior differs from the expected specification and a recorded human decision says the modern app follows the expected specification.
mismatch_decision_pending and specification_decision_pending: a difference, or an undetermined expectation, without an approved decision. Both fail the gate.
gate_rule: Pass only when every scenario unit is a match without a decision record, or a mismatch covered by a decided migration decision (approved_divergence for follow_expected_specification, mismatch_replicate_legacy for replicate_legacy_behavior); the decision registry has no errors (unknown or duplicate entries, defect candidates that differ from the Ground Truth, decided entries without decided_by, decided_at or rationale, decisions on undetermined expectations); and every executed boundary case matches. A mismatch without a record, a pending decision, an undetermined expectation, a record whose unit now matches, and any execution error fail the gate. Boundary cases that were not executed are reported as not_executed and are not counted as passes.

boundary_cases.note: Cases that were not executed are not counted as passes.

approved_divergences.note: Intentional incompatibilities approved by a recorded migration decision (follow_expected_specification). The Compatibility_Evaluation must report these scenarios as approved divergences: the modern app is expected to differ from the legacy response and to return the approved target. For every other scenario the legacy response stays the reference (R13.3).

scenarios.title: Successful order, no discount, shipping fee applies

expected_specification.derived_from: Seed price 80 x 13 = 1040. Subtotal below 3000 gives discount 0. Net amount 1040 is below 5000, so the shipping fee is 500. Total = 1040 - 0 + 500 = 1540. Stock 1000 - 13 = 987.

scenarios.title: Successful order, highest discount tier (subtotal 10000 or more)

expected_specification.derived_from: Seed price 1200 x 9 = 10800. Subtotal of 10000 or more gives discount 1000. Net amount 9800 is 5000 or more, so the shipping fee is 0. Total = 10800 - 1000 + 0 = 9800. Stock 100 - 9 = 91.

scenarios.title: Successful order, middle discount tier (subtotal 3000 to 9999)

expected_specification.derived_from: Seed price 150 x 20 = 3000. Subtotal 3000 gives discount 300. Net amount 2700 is below 5000, so the shipping fee is 500. Total = 3000 - 300 + 500 = 3200. Stock 500 - 20 = 480.

scenarios.title: Successful order, free shipping (net amount 5000 or more)

expected_specification.derived_from: Seed price 800 x 7 = 5600. Subtotal 5600 gives discount 300. Net amount 5300 is 5000 or more, so the shipping fee is 0. Total = 5600 - 300 + 0 = 5300. Stock 50 - 7 = 43.

scenarios.title: Order rejected: subtotal below the minimum order value

expected_specification.derived_from: Seed price 80 x 12 = 960, which is below the minimum of 1000. No order is created and stock is unchanged.

Product 5 has stock 50 and 51 are requested. The request is rejected, product 5 is identified with its current stock (available 50) and the requested quantity (requested 51), no order is created and stock is unchanged. available and requested were added to the specification by the project owner approval (R3.9, R5.2); they were not copied from legacy output.
Product 999 does not exist. The request is rejected, the unrecognised identifier is reported, and no order is created.
Customer 999 is not in the customer master. The request is rejected, no order is created and stock is unchanged.
Product 5 stock is 50. An order for 3 reserves 3 (stock 47). Cancelling restores 3, so the confirmation reports product 5 with stock 50 and the order status becomes cancelled.

scenarios.title: Cancellation rejected: order is already cancelled

expected_specification.derived_from: A second cancellation of the same order is rejected as already cancelled and changes no data. Stock stays at 50.

scenarios.title: Cancellation rejected: order does not exist

expected_specification.derived_from: Order 99999 does not exist. The request is rejected as not found and changes no data.

scenarios.title: Reset is repeatable and restores the seeded state

expected_specification.derived_from: The first reset removes the 1 order and 1 order line and restores the 5 seed products. The second reset has nothing left to delete. After each reset the state is the seeded state.

expected.reason: A zero subtotal cannot be produced by a valid order line. Every product price is at least 1 yen (legacy/sql/schema.sql declares CHECK (unit_price BETWEEN 1 AND 9999999); MySQL 5.7 parses but does not enforce CHECK, so this is the declared domain) and every quantity must be a positive integer (R3.13), so each valid line contributes at least 1 yen and any valid order has a subtotal of at least 1. A subtotal of 0 would need quantity 0, which is itself invalid input (DC-001, SCN-015), an empty line list, which is rejected as an invalid request (R3.10), or a 0-yen product outside the declared price domain; none of these tests the rule. The values are the rule outputs only. Reason approved by the project owner; the CHECK constraint is declared but not enforced by MySQL 5.7.
